title: Add Create Playlist button to Your Content pane
summary: The **Your content** screen (reached from your profile) now has a **+ Create** button to the left of the filter chips (All, Annotations, Highlights, Saves, Playlists). It opens a small menu with one option, **Playlist**, which closes Your content and opens the playlist editor on a new, empty playlist, so you can start a playlist without leaving to find the Discover pane first.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If it shows an error or doesn't load, wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the normal site, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

setup.title: Know how to reach Your content
setup.body: Open your profile: on a wide window, click your **profile picture / initials** in the left sidebar (it says **Open profile** when you hover over it); on a phone-sized window, tap **You** in the bottom bar. On the profile screen, choose **Your content** ("Create and manage your content"). The tests below call this "open **Your content**".

tests.title: The Create button shows before the filter chips
steps: Open **Your content**.
Look at the row just below the search box.
expected: A filled, pill-shaped **+ Create** button is at the left of the row.
The filter chips (**All**, **Annotations**, **Highlights**, **Saves**, **Playlists**) follow it on the same row.
The button looks like the **+ Create** button at the top of the Discover pane (same filled color and rounded shape).

tests.title: The Create menu offers only Playlist
steps: Open **Your content**.
Click **+ Create**.
expected: A small menu opens with exactly one option: **Playlist**, with a music-list icon.
There's no **Annotation** option (unlike the Discover pane's Create menu).
tests.why: The PR only adds Playlist here on purpose. If you think Annotation should also be offered, note it.

tests.title: Choosing Playlist opens the editor on a new, empty playlist
steps: Open **Your content**.
Click **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
expected: The Your content screen and the profile screen both close.
The playlist editor opens in the Discover pane, with an empty title (showing **Untitled playlist** or a blank title box), no description and **No items yet.**
No other screen is left covering the editor.

tests.title: A playlist made from Your content saves and shows up there
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, with the new playlist open in the editor.
steps: Type `Create button test` as the playlist title.
Click **Add item** and add any passage (for example **John 3**), then confirm adding it.
Click **Save**.
Open **Your content** again and click the **Playlists** chip.
expected: The playlist saves without an error.
**Create button test** is listed under Playlists.

tests.title: Closing the menu without choosing does nothing
steps: Open **Your content**.
Click **+ Create** to open the menu.
Click on an empty part of the screen, or press **Esc**.
expected: The menu closes.
You're still on Your content, and no playlist editor opened.

tests.title: Cancelling a new playlist leaves nothing behind
steps: Open **Your content**, click **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
Without typing anything, click **Cancel** in the editor (if asked about unsaved changes, choose to discard them).
Open **Your content** again and click the **Playlists** chip.
expected: No new empty or **Untitled playlist** appears in the list.

setup.title: Use a phone, or a phone-sized window
setup.body: Open the preview on a phone, or make your browser window narrow (about the width of a phone). On a phone, sign in the same way.

tests.title: On a phone, the Create button stays put while the chips scroll
steps: Open **Your content** (tap **You** in the bottom bar, then **Your content**).
Look at the row with **+ Create** and the chips.
Swipe the chips sideways to the left.
expected: **+ Create** and the chips fit on one line; nothing wraps to a second line and the text in the button isn't cut off or squashed.
The chips scroll sideways, and you can reach **Playlists** at the end.
**+ Create** doesn't scroll away; it stays at the left.
The whole page does not scroll sideways.

tests.title: Creating a playlist works on a phone
steps: Open **Your content**.
Tap **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
expected: The playlist editor opens on a new, empty playlist and fills the screen properly; you aren't left on the profile or Your content screen.

tests.title: The Create button is readable in dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode (in Settings, or switch your device to dark mode).
Open **Your content**.
expected: The **+ Create** button's text is easy to read against its background color, in both light and dark mode.
Hovering over it (on a computer) only dims it slightly; it doesn't turn a different color or lose its text.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The filter chips still filter your content
steps: Open **Your content**.
Click each chip in turn: **Annotations**, **Highlights**, **Saves**, **Playlists**, then **All**.
expected: The chip you clicked is shown as selected, and the list changes to show only that kind of content (or a message such as "Playlists you create will show up here." if you have none).

tests.title: Editing an existing playlist from Your content still works
tests.before: You need a playlist, such as **Create button test** from earlier.
steps: Open **Your content** and click the **Playlists** chip.
Open the **Playlist options** menu (⋮) on **Create button test** and choose **Edit playlist**.
expected: Your content closes and the editor opens with that playlist's title and items, not an empty playlist.

tests.title: The Discover pane's Create button still works
steps: Close any open screens and open the **Discover** pane.
Click **+ Create** at the top of the Discover pane.
expected: The menu shows both **Annotation** and **Playlist**, and choosing **Playlist** opens a new, empty playlist.

notCovered: Creating a playlist while signed out: Your content is reached from the signed-in profile screen, so a tester can't normally get there signed out. The code asks the person to sign in if it ever happens.
Other languages: the button and menu reuse the existing "Create" and "Playlist" text from the Discover pane, so no new translations were added.
The automated tests added in the PR (button position, menu contents, and that choosing Playlist starts a new playlist).
